brown trout.line: Speckled gold and red, hard as a fist in the hand. He fought the whole way in.

perch.line: Barred green with that spiked dorsal up like a raised hackle. Handsome and furious.

roach.line: Silver with red fins, the commonest fish in the water and none the worse for it.

rudd.line: Brassy gold, feeding right at the surface in the last of the light.

gudgeon.line: Tiny, whiskered, entirely unbothered. The smallest catch in the river and somehow the most pleased with itself.

eel.line: All muscle and no manners. Came out of the dark under the bank and made a knot of the line.

pike.line: The wolf of the river. Green-barred, ancient-eyed, and it looked at you before it went back down.

salmon.line: Came up out of the deep pool under the willow like something coming home. Sea-bright. A long way from where it started.

a river stone.line: Not a fish. A stone, greenish-blue and worn perfectly round, the exact colour of Blair. Worth keeping anyway.

an old boot.line: One boot. Left foot. Full of river. There is no story attached and that is somehow worse.

something silver.line: It caught the moon on the way up and you have not been able to name it since. It is warm, which river things are not.
